​
“In response to these crimes, during the 17th wave of Operation Nasr-2 (Victory-2) under the blessed code ‘Ya Sahib al-Zaman Adrikni,’ the depot of US unmanned vessels in Bahrain was crushed in the early hours of today, and a large number of them burned in the fire,” one of the statements read.
​
The IRGC also said it had “completely destroyed” Bahrain’s main artificial intelligence center, which had been used in targeting operations for US war crimes.
​
The statement warned that if the United States continued attacking bridges and transportation infrastructure, Iran would target “the most important industrial, information technology and artificial intelligence assets of companies with American shareholders” across the region, adding that “all countries hosting US bases in the region are partners in these war crimes.”
​
In a separate statement, the IRGC Navy said four “violating” vessels attempted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz with the backing of the “terrorist US army.”
​
It said a combined missile and drone operation forced all four vessels to stop in place, warning shipowners not to rely on unfounded US military support and urging them to heed IRGC naval warnings.
​
In another statement, the IRGC said two oil tankers attempting to pass through a mined route south of the Strait of Hormuz “under deception by US intelligence organizations” exploded and caught fire.
​
The statement declared that the Strait of Hormuz had become “highly insecure and completely closed” because of US actions, adding that “until the aggressions of criminal America end, the export of chemical fertilizer and even a single drop of oil and gas from this region will not be possible.”
​
It warned all vessels not to enter the mined route in order to protect lives and property.

Strategy finally sold Bitcoin

For years, Strategy has been buying Bitcoin with money raised from investors, promising them regular payouts.

Roughly speaking, it's similar to bonds: you lend money to the company, and in return you receive a fixed payment in U.S. dollars every quarter.

This week, one of those payments came due, but the company didn't have enough cash on hand. For the first time, it sold part of its Bitcoin holdings — 3,588 BTC, for about $216 million.

Technically, that's just 0.4% of its total Bitcoin holdings, which isn't much. However, the company's payment obligations continue to grow.

And if the company ultimately changes its approach and begins selling off its Bitcoin holdings, it could easily become the trigger for a deep correction in the crypto market.

For context, a sale of $200 million was enough to trigger a 2.5% decline. At the moment, the company still holds about $53 billion worth of Bitcoin on its balance sheet.
